values: TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS | Stack, deployment, security, support and open decisions
Backend on Python 3.12 with FastAPI, Uvicorn, async SQLAlchemy 2.x and Pydantic v2; typed REST JSON APIs.
Service starts, passes health check and serves documented endpoints.
PostgreSQL as the system of record (prototype runs 18) with exact NUMERIC amounts, append-only audit triggers and Alembic migrations applied on start.
Migrations apply and roll back cleanly; audit tables reject update and delete.
Frontend on Next.js 16, React 19 and TypeScript with the navy design tokens in light, dark and system themes.
Production build succeeds; screens render in all themes.
AI models called through Anthropic Claude API or Claude Agent SDK behind a model gateway with model allow-list; deterministic fallback when no key or model is unavailable.
investigator.py, llm.py; LLM paths untested without a key.
Agents run with and without credentials; failure never blocks deterministic processing.
Ontology consumed through REST and an MCP server (stdio) with versioned, permission-filtered content.
Approved release retrieved; incomplete or revoked context falls back to local catalog.
Durable queues, transactional outbox and a workflow runtime with timers, retries and recovery for long-running cases.
Prototype uses in-process workflow state; design calls for durable runtime.
Workflows resume correctly after restart, retry and partial failure.
Encrypted object storage for raw payloads and evidence packages with retention controls.
Prototype stores payloads in the database.
Originals retrievable by hash; lifecycle and encryption verified.
Shopify Admin API integration with pinned API version, pagination, rate-limit handling and HMAC-verified webhooks; transaction log files accepted as files or exports.
Sync, replay and webhook paths produce identical canonical records.
Bank interface through file (BAI2, CAMT.053, CSV via SFTP) or API, with checksum, completeness marker and schema versioning.
Bank deposits currently pushed through the ingest API only.
Bank files load unattended on schedule and failures raise alerts.
Published OpenAPI contract, versioned endpoints, cursor pagination, consistent error format and health endpoint.
Contract published; breaking changes require a version increment.
Container images for backend and frontend, with Docker Compose for local development.
New developer runs the stack with one command.

Production hosting on Microsoft Azure using managed services: Front Door (TLS, routing, CDN), Linux App Service hosting the Next.js frontend and API backend, Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Blob Storage, Key Vault, Azure Monitor with Application Insights, DNS and a container registry; defined as infrastructure as code.
Prototype runs on Docker Compose. Azure chosen; region and data residency still open.
Environment is reproducible from code in a clean account.
Separate development, test, UAT / staging and production environments, each with its own application, database and storage, and isolated data, credentials and configuration.
No cross-environment credentials or data; promotion is the only path to production.
CI/CD pipeline: build, unit and integration tests, vulnerability scan, artifact versioning, gated promotion and automated rollback.
Every merge is built and tested; production deploy needs approval and can roll back.
Configuration through environment variables and a secrets manager; no secrets in source, images or logs; webhook secrets not stored in plain text.
Env-driven config exists; webhook secrets stored in database in the demo.
Secret scan clean; rotation without redeploy.
Network design: TLS termination, private database, web application firewall, restricted CORS and outbound allow-list to Shopify, bank, ontology and model endpoints.
CORS list configured; no network layer defined.
Only required ingress and egress open; verified by scan.
Scheduled daily batch run by a managed scheduler with exit codes, alerting on failure and safe rerun.
batch_job.py supports date, rerun and exit codes.
Missed or failed runs alert within the agreed window.

Capacity baseline: 50,000 transactions a day (about 1.5 million a month, 18.25 million a year), 100 GB of audit evidence files, about 1 million requests and 50 GB of client transfer a month. Load tests must cover peak and batch ingestion when many sources load together, not only the average rate of about 0.6 transactions a second; transaction lines and attachments can multiply storage.
Action Center tested at 200,000 cases (queries under 0.3s); sizing baseline from the Azure brief.
Load test meets agreed targets at peak and batch volume; storage growth projected per line item.

Availability tiers: a baseline with one application instance and managed database backups, and a high-availability tier with two App Service instances (built-in load balancing) and a zone-redundant PostgreSQL standby for stricter service levels; no self-managed proxy VM.
Azure brief; baseline accepts short maintenance and recovery windows.
Tier selected per client SLA; failover tested for the high-availability tier.
Optional network hardening when required: Web Application Firewall, Private Endpoints with VNet integration and a fixed outbound IP for partner allow-lists.
Raised only if the client requires it.
Controls verified by a scan and a connectivity test.
Single sign-on through the Ontology Studio identity (JWT verification per request) with a production identity provider and role mapping.
auth.py verifies tokens against Ontology Studio.
Users sign in with corporate identity; roles and store scope arrive in claims.
Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest with managed keys; quarterly credential rotation and audited secret access.
Dependency and image vulnerability scanning, static analysis and an independent penetration test before go-live.
No open critical or high findings at release.

Azure administration: MFA and least-privilege roles for administrators; secrets, keys and certificates in Key Vault; HTTPS and PostgreSQL TLS enforced; database firewall rules, moving to private access when required.
Access review clean; no secrets outside Key Vault.

Monitoring: metrics, structured logs, traces and dashboards for ingestion, matching, cases, agents and connectors, with alerts for API failures, database CPU and storage, backup usage, slow queries and unusual log ingestion.
/api/health, audit events and agent telemetry exist.
Alerts fire for failed batch, stale data, connector errors and agent failures.

Support model agreed with the client: tiers (L1, L2, L3), coverage hours, escalation matrix, incident severities with response and resolution targets, and the optional Azure support plan and Microsoft escalation path.
Signed support schedule and on-call roster.

Cost and log governance: cost budgets with alerts at 50%, 80% and 100% of the monthly budget, log sampling and severity thresholds with short retention, size limits on uploaded evidence, and scaling ceilings.
Budget alerts fire in test; log ingestion stays within target.
Compliance assurance: confirm data residency, retention, privacy, tax, financial-record and PCI obligations before fixing the region and backup policy.
Runbooks for batch failure, stale data, connector outage, quarantine handling, database restore, agent disable and credential rotation.
Troubleshooting table in DATA_PIPELINE_AND_CONFIGURATION.md is a start.
Each runbook walked through in a drill.

Backup and restore: PostgreSQL automatic backups with point-in-time restore, Blob soft delete and versioning, Hot to Cool to Archive lifecycle, long-term retention vault and geo or second-region recovery where contractually required, monitored backup and log-storage usage, documented RPO and RTO and a restore test at least quarterly.
Not defined; backup behaviour from the Azure brief.
Restore test meets RPO and RTO; backup usage alert tested.
Release management: semantic versioning, change calendar, release notes, hotfix path and rollback procedure.
Releases follow the agreed calendar with notes.
Hypercare after go-live (suggested four weeks) with daily review of cases, batch results and agent outcomes, then handover to run support.
Exit criteria met and signed off.
Documentation and training: administrator guide, Finance and IT user guides, API and integration guides, configuration reference.
Guides reviewed by users and kept current with releases.
Data retention and archive jobs per policy; agent run logs kept 90 days (failures 1 year, audit 7 years).
Retention policy, preview and archive implemented.
LLM usage and spend monitoring with per-investigation cap and per-batch case limits, with alerts on budget breach.
Spend reported by day and model; breach alerts tested.
End-to-end traceability: correlation and causation IDs carried across ingestion, case, workflow, agent run, tool call and export, with distributed tracing into Azure Monitor.
Audit events already hold correlation and case links; no tracing layer.
Any case can be traced from source record to export in one view.
Alert routing and synthetic checks: severity-based routing to on-call, runbook links, and scheduled health checks for sign-in, ingestion, batch run and exports.
/api/health and batch status exist; no routing.
A failed check pages the right owner within the agreed time.
Pipeline observability: per-feed counts (received, archived, quarantined, matched, exceptions), freshness windows and late-arrival or quarantine alerts.
Pipeline page and feed health implemented; no alerting.
Overdue feed or quarantine spike alerts in test.

Agent run record: agent type and version, prompt version, model, ontology context identity, tokens, duration, each tool call with status, result status and policies checked, searchable in a run-trace view.
Agent runs audited with ontology context; run trace not a screen.
An investigator can replay what an agent saw, called and concluded.
Prompt and response retention for audit: store the prompts, tool results and outputs needed to explain a decision, with field masking, auditor-only access and retention by policy.
Design requires explainable provenance, not hidden reasoning.
Sample run reconstructed from stored records; masked fields verified.

Agent quality monitoring in production: sampled scoring of groundedness, citation rejection, false-support rate, refusal on missing evidence and contradictions; scheduled evaluation runs on labelled scenarios; alert on drift after a model or prompt change.
Evaluation harness and shadow-mode report exist.
Quality metrics trend visible; release blocked when thresholds fail.
Agent safety alerts: policy violations, unauthorized-action attempts and instruction-injection attempts raise a critical alert, block the output and are reported as attempted, blocked and executed.
Required by agent guardrails in the design.
Agent SLO dashboards: investigation success rate, latency, evidence-retrieval success and validation accuracy with alert thresholds, alongside token and spend usage.
Targets defined in the agent design; no dashboards.
Dashboards live and thresholds alert in test.
Human feedback loop: shadow-mode agreement, rejected or overridden recommendations and reasons captured and added to the evaluation sets.
Shadow report exists; feedback not fed back.
Overrides appear in the next evaluation run.

Audit integrity: scheduled hash-chain verification with an alert on any break, periodic anchoring of the chain head in an external immutable store, and an application database role without update or delete rights.
Chain and verify endpoint exist; README notes external anchoring is needed for stronger guarantees.
A tampered row is detected and alerted; anchored head matches after restore.

Audit coverage: sign-in, authorization denials, configuration and policy changes, impersonation, exports, administrator actions and reads of sensitive evidence, each with actor, time, before and after state and reason.
Case, decision, agent, export and settings events audited; reads and denials not.
Coverage matrix reviewed and tested against each event class.
Auditor access: read-only auditor role, search and filter, export with hashes and time-bounded evidence packages, with segregation so administrators cannot alter audit records.
Auditor role and audit export exist.
External audit request satisfied without engineering help.
Optional forwarding of audit and security events to the client SIEM, with synchronized clocks across services.
Raised only if the client requires it.
Events arrive in the SIEM with correct timestamps.
Automated test tooling: pytest and agent evaluation harness (present), plus frontend component, end-to-end and load tests.
Test suite runs in CI and gates merges.
Engineering standards: linting, formatting, type checking, code review, branch strategy and definition of done.
Checks run automatically on every change.
Azure region and data-residency obligations (provider chosen: Azure).
Region changes pricing and availability; needed before infrastructure design.
Durable workflow runtime and message broker choice.
Production identity provider and whether Ontology Studio remains the authentication authority.
Prototype depends on Ontology Studio availability.
Shopify export mechanism (API, scheduled export file or both) and bank interface method and format.
Support hours, response targets and who provides L1 and L2 after hypercare.
Uptime target, recovery-time objective (RTO) and recovery-point objective (RPO).
Design leaves these undefined; they decide the availability tier.
Targets agreed and added to NFRs.
Expected peak ingestion rate, integration method per source, average transaction size and monthly attachment volume.
Needed to size the database and test peak load.
Retention periods for transactions, evidence, logs and backups.
Drives storage tiers and backup policy.
Need for WAF, private networking, single sign-on, fixed IP allow-lists and penetration testing.
Need for separate staging, UAT, training or disaster-recovery environments.
